purpose: Tell a governor what his town should be about
note: Issue 454, SPEC 9.4 'ordering construction' and 8.5: the PC never names a project; he argues for a goal, and the governor's menu chooses what serves it. Composed rather than only answered, so the PC can make the argument unprompted. The same four courses the governors' reports offer, and the same effect. Education is not among them: it is the Provost's to urge. Placeholder prose: the Author writes the real lines.

options.text: on a matter of the town's direction
with every confidence in what you have made of it
because the town has drifted long enough
because the colony cannot afford a town that does nothing in particular

steps.prompt: What the town should be about

options.label: attend to the colony's profit
options.text: Attend to the colony's profit. That is what you are there for, and what the Crown will ask me about.

options.label: see that the town grows
options.text: See that the town grows: people, and the comforts that keep them.

options.label: see to your defences
options.text: See to your defences. I had rather pay for walls than for what comes over them.

options.label: plant a new settlement
options.text: Plant a new settlement. The land is there, and somebody will have it.
